one_line: Founding Satavahana brothers of the western Deccan, early patrons of cave sanctuaries and dynastic rule.

appearance.age_look: Simuka appears in his mid-40s with a solid, broad-shouldered build; Kanha appears early-30s with a slightly leaner but athletic frame.
appearance.face: Both have oval faces with strong jaws and medium-brown Deccan complexions; Simuka has a prominent, slightly aquiline nose, faint forehead lines and calm, authoritative eyes with a steady half-smile, while Kanha has sharper brows, a straighter nose and a more intense, alert gaze; both keep a dignified default expression of composed focus rather than aggression.
appearance.hair: Simuka’s hair is deep black, gathered into a smooth topknot (kaparda-style knot) high on the back of his head with the sides neatly combed, a narrow gold circlet resting just above his forehead; Kanha’s deep black hair is shorter and wavier, pulled into a smaller, tighter knot slightly lower on the head with a plain cloth band in dull red tied around it, a few controlled strands framing his temples.
appearance.costume: Simuka wears a finely draped off-white cotton uttariya (upper cloth) wrapped over both shoulders and crossing the chest diagonally, leaving a modest high neckline, paired with a knee-length dhoti in muted saffron wrapped tightly and pleated in front, bordered with a thin maroon stripe; over this he has a light sleeveless quilted cotton vest in pale beige suggesting padded protection, tied at the side with fabric cords, and a broad cloth girdle in dark maroon around his waist; his ornaments are region-appropriate but restrained—simple round gold earrings, a single medium-thickness gold neck torque, two slim gold bangles on each wrist, and a signet-style ring on his right hand; his feet are in plain brown leather sandals with a toe loop; Kanha wears a darker, more practical version: a deep indigo cotton uttariya draped over the left shoulder and under the right arm, a dull ochre dhoti of similar knee-length with a dark green border, and a short-sleeved, close-fitting cotton tunic in greyish blue beneath the drape; a narrow leather belt with a simple bronze buckle sits over his waist cloth, and he has fewer ornaments—small bronze hoop earrings, a single bead necklace of dark stone, and one bronze bangle on his sword arm; his sandals are darker brown and more rugged, with simple straps across the foot.
appearance.signature: Simuka’s signature prop is a long, slightly curved iron sword (early Deccan-style) with a simple straight crossguard and a dark wooden hilt wrapped in reddish-brown leather, worn in a plain brown scabbard at his left hip, while Kanha’s signature prop is a rolled palm-leaf charter bound with a red cord tucked into his belt, symbolizing administrative grants and cave patronage.

ref_desc: Simuka and Kanha Satavahana are medium-brown Deccan brothers with oval faces, Simuka’s hair in a high black topknot with a gold circlet and Kanha’s in a lower knot with a red band, wearing off-white and saffron dhoti-uttariya with beige quilted vest and indigo-ochre dhoti-uttariya with grey-blue tunic, brown leather sandals, Simuka carrying a plain curved iron sword at his hip and Kanha a rolled palm-leaf charter, in a palette of off-white, muted saffron, deep indigo, maroon and brown leather.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of two historically grounded early Satavahana brothers from the western Deccan, Simuka and Kanha Satavahana, standing side by side so their shared yet distinct designs are clear: both with medium-brown complexions, oval faces and strong jaws; Simuka slightly older, broader-shouldered, with calm authoritative eyes, a faintly lined forehead and a steady half-smile, his deep black hair gathered into a smooth high topknot with the sides neatly combed and a narrow gold circlet resting just above his forehead; Kanha a bit younger and leaner, with sharper brows, an alert intense gaze and deep black hair in a shorter, tighter knot slightly lower on the head tied with a simple dull red cloth band, a few controlled strands framing his temples. Dress Simuka in an off-white cotton uttariya draped over both shoulders and diagonally across the chest to create a modest high neckline, a knee-length muted saffron dhoti tightly wrapped and pleated in front with a thin maroon border, a light sleeveless quilted cotton vest in pale beige suggesting subtle padding tied with side cords, a broad maroon cloth girdle at his waist and plain brown leather sandals with toe loops; give him simple round gold earrings, a single medium-thickness gold neck torque, two slim gold bangles on each wrist and a signet-style ring, and hang his signature long slightly curved iron sword with a straight crossguard and a dark wooden hilt wrapped in reddish-brown leather in a plain brown scabbard at his left hip. Dress Kanha in a deep indigo cotton uttariya draped over the left shoulder and under the right arm, a dull ochre knee-length dhoti with a dark green border, and a close-fitting short-sleeved cotton tunic in greyish blue beneath the drape; add a narrow leather belt with a simple bronze buckle over his waist cloth, darker brown rugged sandals with straps, small bronze hoop earrings, a single dark stone bead necklace and one bronze bangle on his sword arm, and tuck his signature rolled palm-leaf charter bound with a red cord into his belt. Use a cohesive palette of off-white, muted saffron, deep indigo, maroon and brown leather, and show them in neutral, balanced poses from head to toe to clearly display hairstyles, jewellery, drapery, belts, weapons and props without any text or labels.
